tools.name: Glob
tools.description:
Find files by glob pattern, sorted by modification time (most recent first).

Powered by ripgrep. Respects `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.rgignore` by default — set `include_ignored` to also match ignored files (e.g. build outputs, `node_modules`). Sensitive files (such as `.env`) are always filtered out. Matches are files only — directories themselves are never listed; to find a directory, glob for a file inside it (e.g. `**/fixtures/**`).

Good patterns:
- `*.ts` — all files matching an extension, at any depth below the search root (a bare pattern without `/` matches recursively)
- `src/*.ts` — files directly inside `src/` (one level, not recursive)
- `src/**/*.ts` — recursive walk with a subdirectory anchor and extension
- `**/*.py` — recursive walk from the search root for an extension
- `*.{ts,tsx}` — brace expansion is supported
- `{src,test}/**/*.ts` — cartesian brace expansion is supported too

Results are capped at the first 100 matching paths. If a search would return more, a truncation marker is appended. Refine the pattern (extension, subdirectory) when 100 is not enough, or call again with a narrower anchor.

Large-directory caveat — avoid recursing into dependency / build output even with an anchor, especially when `include_ignored` is set:
- `node_modules/**/*.js`, `.venv/**/*.py`, `__pycache__/**`, `target/**` can produce thousands of results that truncate at the match cap and waste context. Prefer specific subpaths like `node_modules/react/src/**/*.js`.

include_ignored.description: Also match files excluded by ignore files such as `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.rgignore` (for example `node_modules` or build outputs). Sensitive files (such as `.env`) remain filtered out for safety. VCS metadata directories (`.git` and similar) are always skipped, even when this is true. Defaults to false.

include_dirs.description: Deprecated and ignored. Results are always files-only — directories are never listed. Accepted only so older calls that still pass this flag are not rejected by parameter validation.

# test18_executable — URL Parser Probe Report

## Interface & output contract

- Usage: `test18_executable <url>`; reads **only argv[1]** (extra args ignored). **No argument → exit 1, no output.** All tested inputs → **exit 0**, never crashes (incl. 15 KB inputs, empty string, malformed input).
- Prints **18 lines** (fields may themselves contain `\n`, so line count can exceed 18):

| # | Field | Notes |
|---|-------|-------|
| 1 | scheme | lowercased; empty if no `://` |
| 2 | authority | **reconstructed** (userinfo@host:port, only valid parts), not raw substring |
| 3 | userinfo | |
| 4 | host | |
| 5 | port | integer, `-1` when absent/invalid |
| 6 | path | |
| 7 | query | |
| 8 | fragment | |
| 9–16 | flags | hasScheme, hasAuthority(≡hasHost in all probes), hasUserInfo, hasHost, hasPort, hasPath, hasQuery, hasFragment — `1` iff component non-empty (port flag iff valid port parsed) |
| 17 | toString | reconstruction, see rules below |
| 18 | valid | `1` iff host or path non-empty; `0` for `""`, `http://`, `?q`, `#f`, `http://?q`, `://` |

## Parsing pipeline (inferred order)

1. Split fragment at **first `#`**; 2. split query at **first `?`** (so `a?b://c/d` → path `a`, query `b://c/d`); 3. in the remaining head, split scheme at **first `://`** — if absent, the whole head is the path (`http:`, `http:/x`, `//h/p`, `http:\\h\p` all become path); 4. authority = up to first `/`; 5. split userinfo at **first `@`**; 6. split port at first `:` in the host part.

## Surprising / migration-critical behaviors

- **Zero validation/normalization of characters**: spaces, tabs, `\r`, `\x0b`, `\x0c`, `\x01`, unicode (`café`, `路径`, `münich.de`) pass through **byte-verbatim** everywhere — no trimming, no encoding, no rejection. `" http://example.com/trailingspace "` → scheme=`" http"` (leading space!), path=`"/trailingspace "`. `\n` has *no* special meaning; it just lands inside a field (path=`"/path\nnewline"`).
- **Percent sequences never decoded or validated**: `/%41%42`, `/%`, `/%zz%`, `/100%`, `%25` in fragment all kept literally, even in host (`ex%41mple.com`).
- **Scheme**: any bytes before `://` accepted (`1http`, `ht+tp.-x`, `!!!http`, `...http`), then **lowercased** (`HTTP`→`http` in both field 1 and toString). Host is **not** lowercased (`HTTP://EXAMPLE.COM/P` → `http://EXAMPLE.COM/P`).
- **Port** is the only validated component — `strtol`-style prefix parse (skips leading space/sign, stops at first non-digit): `:080`→80, `:+80`→80, `: 80`→80, `:80 `→80, `:80x`→80, `:9e9`→9, `:08:90`→8, `:-0`→0. Accepted range **0–65535** (`65535` ok; `65536`, `2147483647`, `-1`, empty, `abc` rejected). **Invalid port is silently erased** from port field, authority field, and toString: `http://host:abc/` → `http://host/`; valid port is **normalized** into output: `http://host:080/` → authority `host:80`, toString `http://host:80/`.
- **Userinfo `@` handling**: first `@` splits, so `a@b@c` → userinfo `a`, host `b@c`; `u@@h` → userinfo `u`, host `@h`; `h:80@u` → userinfo `h:80`, host `u` (@ beats `:`). Empty userinfo drops the `@` (`http://@host/` → `http://host/`), but empty host keeps it (`http://user:pass@/` → authority `user:pass@`, toString unchanged).
- **No IPv6 support**: `http://[::1]:80/p` → host=`[`, port garbage rejected, toString `http://[/p`.
- **Empty scheme + authority is parsed but dropped by toString**: `://u@h:80/p?q#f` → fields host=`h`, port=`80`, etc. all set, but field 17 = `/p?q#f` (authority omitted when scheme empty). `foo://h1://h2/p` → authority `h1`, path `//h2/p`, toString `foo://h1//h2/p` (first `://` wins).
- **Bare delimiters vanish in toString**: `http://h/p?`, `http://h/p#`, `http://h/p?#` all → `http://h/p` (empty query/fragment not re-emitted).
- **toString recipe**: `[scheme + "://" + authority] only if scheme non-empty` + path + `?query` if non-empty + `#fragment` if non-empty. Consequently field 17 ≠ input in many cases (dropped invalid ports, empty userinfo `@`, empty-scheme authorities, bare `?`/`#`, scheme case), yet field 18 stays `1` — 18 is a validity flag, not a round-trip check.
- **Fragment/query precedence**: `#` before `?` wins — `http://h/p#frag?query` → fragment `frag?query`, query empty; `http://h/p??double` → query `?double`; `http://h/p?query#frag#more` → fragment `frag#more`.
- **No length limits**: 10 000-char path, 5 000-char host, 15 KB total all round-trip intact, exit 0.
- **Host characters unvalidated**: `.host.`, `host..com`, `-host-`, `h\p`, tab-containing hosts all accepted as-is.

## Sample normalized 18-field records

`http://user:pass@example.com:8080/p/q?a=b#c` →
`http | user:pass@example.com:8080 | user:pass | example.com | 8080 | /p/q | a=b | c | 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 | http://user:pass@example.com:8080/p/q?a=b#c | 1`

`example.com/path` (no `://`) →
` |  |  |  | -1 | example.com/path |  |  | 0 0 0 0 0 1 0 0 | example.com/path | 1`

`http://host:80x/` →
`http | host:80 |  | host | 80 | / |  |  | 1 1 0 1 1 1 0 0 | http://host:80/ | 1`

`""` → all empty, port `-1`, flags all `0`, toString empty, valid `0`.

**Ambiguity note for the main agent**: flags 10 (hasAuthority) and 12 (hasHost) were identical in every probe — they may be two names for the same condition, or differ in a case I didn't find.
